text.p: Egyptian police have seized the dehydrated body of a boy which may date back more than 2,000 years, a senior antiquities official said on Thursday.
Mohammed Saleh, head of the Egyptian Museum, told Reuters police seized the perfectly-preserved body from a taxi driver who was trying to sell it to antiquities traders for $500,000.
Saleh said preliminary examinations showed that the body, which has traces of red hair, was probably that of an eight-year-old boy and dated back to between the first or sixth century AD.
It did not appear to have been mumified but just preserved under the desert sand, he said.
"The body is in good condition, you can clearly see the features," Saleh said.
A team of experts will run a series of tests on the body to determine its exact age and conditions under which it was buried, Saleh said.
